newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Persson takes aim at EU policy of flexibility.
newsitem.headline: Persson takes aim at EU policy of flexibility.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson urged the European Union on Tuesday to be careful when developing the concept of "flexibility", warning that Europe could otherwise fall apart.

Persson, speaking at a news conference after meeting Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, said that flexibility -- letting groups of states within the EU forge ahead together on matters where others are less enthusiastic -- was somewhat over estimated as a solution ahead of eastern enlargement.
"Some look at it as a solution that will make enlargement possible," Persson said.
"We have to be careful because we can create otherwise a Europe that will fall into parts...Some countries will continue to integrate and some others will stand outside."
Kok said flexibility could be an instrument to make it possible for member states to make progress at different speeds in specified areas of the treaty.
"This has to be done in a careful way," he said. But it should not be a question of creating a Europe "a la carte".
The two leaders also discussed economic and monetary union but refused to speculate on upcoming decisions.
Persson said the Swedish parliament would decide in October or November whether the country should join EMU.
"We are convinced that we will reach the convergence criteria," Persson said.
